Common conditions of pet chinchillas include bite wounds, respiratory diseases, overgrown and impacted teeth, gastrointestinal stasis, bloat, diarrhea, skin problems, reproductive/genital issues, and heat stroke.
These overgrown teeth may start to cut into the tongue, cheek, or lips, leading to difficulty eating, decreased appetite, weight loss, drooling, eye problems, and pawing at the face.
Dental overgrowth commonly occurs in chinchillas that do not eat hay as the main component of their diet.

Gastrointestinal (GI) stasis refers to a slowing down of the passage of food through the stomach and intestines when chinchillas stop eating for several reasons, including dental disease, inappropriate diet, overheating, or other stressors.
Regardless of why the pet stopped eating, GI stasis is a potentially life-threatening condition that must be treated by a veterinarian as soon as possible.
Signs of heat stroke include panting, high body temperature, open-mouthed breathing, and reluctance to move.
Heat stroke is an emergency condition requiring immediate veterinary treatment.

Metabolic bone disease tops the list of health concerns for captive flying squirrels, and it comes down to calcium almost every time. Early signs include wobbliness, reluctance to jump or glide, and general lethargy. Advanced cases involve seizures and fractures from minor activity.
The good news is that it is almost completely preventable through proper diet, and early cases respond well to dietary correction and calcium supplementation under veterinary guidance.

Respiratory infections are the next most common issue, usually caused by dusty bedding, cedar or pine shavings, drafty cage placement, or bacterial exposure. Symptoms include sneezing, wheezing, nasal discharge, and labored breathing.
Cedar and pine shavings are off the table entirely because the aromatic oils cause respiratory problems.
Flying squirrels are small enough that respiratory infections can become serious quickly, so get to your exotic vet at the first signs rather than waiting to see if it resolves on its own.
